headline: A 2014 law changes the default investment for new Thrift Savings Plan participants from the G Fund to an age-based L Fund, with exceptions and added protections.
what_it_does: When a Thrift Savings Plan participant has not chosen how to invest, their money will now go into an age-appropriate target date L Fund instead of the Government Securities Investment Fund (G Fund). Participants whose default is an L Fund must receive a risk acknowledgement before they enroll. Members of the uniformed services keep the G Fund as their default. The law also extends certain fiduciary protection requirements to TSP beneficiaries.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees enrolled in the Thrift Savings Plan who have not made an investment choice
who_it_affects.how: Their contributions will default to an age-appropriate L Fund instead of the G Fund.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the uniformed services in the Thrift Savings Plan
who_it_affects.how: Their default investment stays in the G Fund.

who_it_affects.group: Newly enrolling TSP participants whose default is an L Fund
who_it_affects.how: They must receive a risk acknowledgement before enrolling.
Certain fiduciary protection requirements now apply to them.
